# Tendkit

> Customer support you own: a shared inbox, tickets and a customer portal that you copy into your own app with the shadcn CLI. Customer emails, WhatsApp and SMS become tickets your team answers next to the customer's account. MIT licensed.

Tendkit targets Next.js (App Router), Tailwind 4, shadcn/ui, TanStack Query and Drizzle (Postgres, or SQLite/Cloudflare D1). Channel adapters use only fetch and WebCrypto, so they run on Cloudflare Workers, Node, Bun and Deno.

## Install

`npx shadcn@latest add https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/r/support.json https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/r/support-postgres.json https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/r/support-ui.json https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/r/channel-resend.json`

Registry items: support (core), support-postgres, support-d1, support-ai (optional AI engine), support-ai-postgres, support-ai-d1, support-ui, channel-resend, channel-microsoft365, channel-gmail, channel-smtp, channel-twilio, channel-whatsapp, channel-telegram, channel-api. Each is at https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/r/<item>.json.

## How to integrate (for coding agents)

1. Install the items above with the shadcn CLI (server items into the API package, support-ui into the web app in a monorepo).
2. Export the support schema from the Drizzle schema and generate a migration. Don't apply migrations without asking.
3. Create the service with createSupport({ store, storage, channels, directory, notify, acknowledgement, fromName, portalChannelId, ignoreFrom, team, teamEmail, replyAll }).
4. Implement the SupportDirectory: identify (sender to user and customer/account), searchCustomers, getCustomers, listAgents. This is the only product-specific part.
5. Route POST /api/webhooks/support/[channel] to support().handleWebhook(channel, request). Call support().runScheduled() from a cron every few minutes.
6. Expose the agent methods (listTickets, getTicket, reply, addNote, assign, setStatus, linkCustomer, changeContact, uploadAttachment, attachmentUrl, counts, listAgents, searchCustomers) and support().portal through the app's own API behind its own auth; implement SupportClient with them and render SupportInbox/SupportTicket inside SupportProvider.
7. Optional AI (triage, one-line summaries, suggested replies; agents review and send, except on topics the team switches to Autopilot): add support-ai-postgres or support-ai-d1, export the ai-schema and migrate, then pass ai: supportAi({ model, store: createPostgresAiStore(db), knowledge: [docsFromUrl("https://…/llms-full.txt")], defer }) to createSupport. model is any Vercel AI SDK LanguageModel; Tendkit imports only the "ai" package. Add describeCustomer(customerId) to the directory for account facts. Expose support().ai (refine, writeUp, translate, draft, discardSuggestion, setInsight, getSettings, updateSettings, syncKnowledge, listKnowledgeSources) and put the same methods under ai on the SupportClient; map the inbox's sort: "priority" to listTickets. Customer messages go to the configured model provider. Voice in the reply box (one microphone button; an empty box takes spoken notes through writeUp, a box with text takes a spoken change through refine, or "Insert as spoken" for plain dictation; Escape cancels, Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Space toggles, two-minute limit): pass transcriptionModel (any AI SDK TranscriptionModel) and optionally transcriptionOptions: ({ language }) => providerOptions to supportAi, expose support().ai.transcribe({ audio, language? }) => { text, language } (audio is a Blob, Uint8Array or ArrayBuffer up to 10 MB, never stored) and add the optional transcribe({ audio: Blob }) to client.ai. Without client.ai.transcribe the screens use the browser's Web Speech API in the SupportProvider locale; with neither the button is hidden. A transcription model is more accurate for languages such as Arabic and French. When the browser listens, it uses SupportProvider's speechLocale (default: locale); pass a region such as "fr-FR" when the UI locale is bare "fr". Memory (needs the 0002_memory migration; every client method is optional and the screens hide what's missing): approved answers are the drafts' most trusted source, cited as { type: "answer" }, and agents insert one by typing "/" at the start of a line in the reply box, with {name}, {company} and {agent} filled in and no model call. Expose support().ai.listApprovedAnswers(), generaliseAnswer({ ticketId, text }) => { title, text, language } (takes the customer's details out of a reply for review), saveApprovedAnswer({ id?, title, text, language?, ticketId?, gapId?, actorId }), deleteApprovedAnswer(id), listGuidanceSuggestions(), decideGuidanceSuggestion({ id, accept, rule?, actorId }), listGaps(), dismissGap({ id, actorId }) and draftArticle({ gapId } | { ticketIds }) => { title, markdown }, and add the same names to client.ai (the client passes { id } objects; the server adds actorId). Drafts an agent edits before sending are kept: the same customer's earlier replies go into that customer's later drafts as they were sent; other customers only ever get a one-sentence style note that is dropped if it holds a digit, link, name from the ticket or five words in a row from the conversation (shareStyleNotes: false keeps every correction within its customer). runScheduled draws those notes on each run and, once a day, proposes guidance rules from heavily edited drafts (never applied until a person accepts) and files unanswered questions (cannot_answer suggestions and discarded drafts) under gaps. supportAi also takes an optional embedder: { embed(texts) => number[][] } to order found corrections by meaning. Actions (needs the 0003_actions migration; every client method is optional): pass actions: [supportAction({ name, title, description, input, approval?, run, available?, timeoutMs? })] to supportAi. name is lowercase letters, digits and underscores; input is a Zod schema, any Standard Schema or the AI SDK's jsonSchema() describing an object; approval is "always" (default: an agent approves every run) or "never" (read-only lookups only); run({ input, ticket, customer, contact, agent, signal }) returns { ok, summary, data? } and is always called with the ticket's own customer, never one the model chose; tickets not linked to a customer have no actions. While drafting, the model may call "never" actions through AI SDK tool calling (up to 6 per draft) and cites each as a source { type: "action", title, detail }. Calling an "always" action from a draft only records a proposal on the suggestion (suggestion.actions: { name, title, input, reason, state: proposed | running | done | failed | declined, fields, run }): nothing a customer writes can run a change. Expose support().ai.ticketActions({ ticketId }) as client.ai.listActions, runAction({ ticketId, action, input, actorId, suggestionId?, text? }) => { run, text } (actorId is the signed-in agent from your server; with suggestionId it approves a proposal once, idempotently; text is the reply box, returned rewritten when the agent changed the inputs), declineAction({ ticketId, suggestionId, action, actorId, text? }) => { text } (the reply rewritten without the action), setActionEnabled({ name, enabled }) (lookups only: stops AI running one on its own; "always" can't be changed from the UI), listActions() (add its result as actions to client.ai.getSettings()) and listActionRuns({ ticketId }). Every run is logged in support_action_runs (approvedBy, input, status: succeeded | failed | timed_out | errored, summary, durationMs) and approved or manual runs add an "action_run" event to the agents' timeline. Runs time out after timeoutMs (default 15000). The screens show proposed actions as cards under the suggested reply (Approve, Skip, editable inputs), ask before sending a reply with undecided proposals, and list available actions in the ticket's menu with a form built from the schema. Autopilot (needs the 0004_autopilot migration, which also backfills topic, language and change on existing support_suggestions; every client method is optional): topics a team switches on are answered with no agent reading first. Nothing is on by default and nothing switches itself on. Track record per topic over windowDays (30): decided drafts split into sent as drafted, lightly edited (editWeight < 0.15: the share of words changed, and at least 0.5 whenever a number, link or email address was added, removed or replaced), rewritten, discarded, came back unhappy (sent as drafted or lightly edited, then the customer's next message was frustrated, angry or said it didn't help) and flagged; plus cannot_answer, sent by Autopilot, reopened, and a split by language. A topic is eligible when its latest minDrafts (30) decided drafts are at least minRate (0.9) sent as drafted or lightly edited and no flagged reply awaits review. Configure with supportAi({ autopilot: { minDrafts, minRate, windowDays, holdMinutes: 10, maxPerHour: 30, blockMoods: ["angry"], blockUrgencies: ["urgent"], maxCustomerMessages: 3, minLanguageDrafts: 5, channels?: string[] (default: every email channel), signature?: false | string | ({ language }) => string, canManage?: (agentId) => boolean } }) or autopilot: false to remove it. The team can only raise minDrafts and minRate from the UI. Expose support().ai.getAutopilot() => { stopped, stoppedBy, stoppedAt, minDrafts, minRate, floor, windowDays, holdMinutes, maxPerHour, sentLastHour, topics: [{ topic, stage: collecting | eligible | on | paused, mode: hold | immediate | null, enabledBy, enabledAt, pausedAt, pauseReason: quality | flagged | null, ready, record }] }, setAutopilotTopic({ topic, on, mode?, actorId }) (switching on or resuming is refused unless the record is eligible; who and when are stored; needs canManage), setAutopilot({ stopped?, minDrafts?, minRate?, actorId }) (the kill switch: any agent can stop, restarting and thresholds need canManage), autopilotExamples({ topic, only?: "changed", limit? }), holdAutopilotReply({ suggestionId, actorId }) and flagAutopilotReply({ suggestionId, actorId, note? }); add the same names to client.ai (the server adds actorId). Modes: "hold" stores the suggestion with autopilot: "held" and sendAt = now + holdMinutes, and runScheduled sends it when due unless an agent stopped it, answered, left a note, changed the status, or the customer wrote again; "immediate" sends as soon as it is drafted. A held reply is claimed atomically (held to sending, one conditional update) before it is sent, stopped, or replaced by an agent's reply, so a customer never gets two; reply() throws "Autopilot has just answered this message" while Autopilot is sending or once it sent the draft the agent started from. A reply is sent only if all hold: the topic is on and Autopilot isn't stopped; the ticket is linked to a customer; the channel is allowed; the model set confident: true, every cited source resolved and at least one is not guidance; no action was proposed; mood not in blockMoods and urgency not in blockUrgencies; the customer didn't ask for a person (triage asksForHuman) or say the last reply didn't help (triage notHelped, or came back unhappy after the last suggested reply); fewer than maxCustomerMessages customer messages since the ticket was opened or reopened; the topic has minLanguageDrafts decided drafts in the customer's language at minRate; fewer than maxPerHour sent in the last hour. Otherwise it stays an ordinary suggestion with suggestion.autopilotBlock (stopped, unknown_customer, channel, asked_for_human, not_helped, mood, urgency, long_thread, needs_approval, not_confident, unsourced, language, hourly_cap, held_back, moved_on, send_failed). ai.draft() never sends. A sent reply has authorId null, is signed with fromName and "This reply was sent automatically. If it doesn't help, reply to say so and a person will take over." (never a person's name; left off when the channel has no room), leaves the ticket in "waiting", records suggestion status "used" with autopilot: "sent", and adds an "autopilot_sent" event { messageId, suggestionId, topic, mode } that only agents see. Brakes: flagAutopilotReply pauses the topic (pauseReason "flagged"), reopens the ticket, adds an "autopilot_flagged" event and the question is filed as a gap by the next daily review; a topic whose latest drafts fall under minRate (judged from 10 drafts) pauses with pauseReason "quality", checked before each send and on each runScheduled; setAutopilot({ stopped: true }) stops everything, held replies included. Topic switches live in support_autopilot_topics. The screens: SupportAiSettings shows each topic's readiness, numbers and drafts; the ticket marks the reply "Sent by Autopilot · <topic>" with "Flag as wrong", and shows a held reply with when it goes and "Stop and edit".
8. For email: use a receiving subdomain (e.g. in.acme.com) for the reply address, keep the main mailbox where it is, and copy mail to the receiving address. The Resend adapter needs a Full access API key to read received mail.

- [Introduction](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs)
- [Installation](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/installation): registry entry, items, tables, monorepos
- [The service](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/service): createSupport options, storage, notifications, methods, errors
- [Your directory](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/directory): identify, searchCustomers, getCustomers, listAgents, trust
- [Webhooks and scheduling](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/webhooks): the route, responses, runScheduled
- [Inbox and tickets](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/screens): SupportClient, SupportProvider props, translations
- [Customer portal](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/portal)
- [Theming](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/theming)
- [AI](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/ai): supportAi options, providers, knowledge sources, account facts, deferral, client.ai, voice, memory (approved answers, learning from edits, guidance suggestions, gaps, articles), actions (lookups, proposed actions with approval, manual runs, safety), autopilot (track record, eligibility, hold or immediate, the checks a reply passes, flag, automatic pause, kill switch), privacy
- [Email setup](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/email): receiving domains, threading, trimming, automatic mail, authentication
- [Channels](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/channels): resend, microsoft365, gmail, smtp, twilio, whatsapp, telegram, api, and writing your own (/docs/channels/<name>)
- [Upgrading](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/upgrading)
- [Live demo](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/demo)
